Kai: Observed weird quality dip when enabling speculative batching on redwood-7b-quant for short QA prompts. p50 latency improved but answer correctness fell ~8%.

Maya: is this the same speculative implementation as the other canaries? sampling config?

Kai: yes, speculative_batching enabled, batch_size=32, sampling temp=0.2 top_k=40. Dataset: qa_short_2k.

Jon: low temp -> greedy-ish. did you check deterministic baseline?

Kai: Compared to greedy topk=1 we still lose accuracy. Looks like batching may be mixing KV contexts when prefix lengths vary.

Maya: can you drop a quick eval command?

Kai: ```bash
rwictl eval run \
  --model redwood-7b-4bit \
  --decoding speculative_batch \
  --batch 32 \
  --sampling '{"temp":0.2,"top_k":40}' \
  --evalset qa_short_2k \
  --metrics exact_match,accuracy,latency
```

CI Bot: job 777 created and queued.

Jon: capture per-request effective prefix length distribution and any KV collision logs.

Kai: will do. also plan ablation with batch_size=8 and with batching disabled.

Maya: thanks — aim to have verdict by EOD. if accuracy doesn't recover, disable speculative_batch on 7b-4bit.
